_readme: Add-on sections the trip wizard merges into the chosen template (docs/WIZARD.md). Each module: id, title (the section it adds or merges into), why (shown on the review step), items {text, required, note?, permitRequired?}, and optional removeItems (regular expressions, case-insensitive) applied to the template first.

items.text: Kid-sized sleeping bags and pads
Comfort item (stuffed animal, blanket)
Headlamp or glow sticks for each kid
Double the clothes for little ones (plus swim and mud sets)
Children's medicines, thermometer, kid sunscreen and bug spray
Snacks that travel well
Games, books, cards, a ball
Whistle on a lanyard and a 'stay put if lost' talk
Dog food for every day plus one, and bowls
Leash (6 ft for most parks) and a tie-out or long line
Waste bags
Vaccination records and ID tags
items.note: Check the park's dog rules: many trails and all backcountry areas in national parks are closed to dogs.

items.text: Dog bed or blanket
Towel and a brush or tick comb
Extra water and a collapsible bowl for hikes
Treats and a favourite toy
Dog first-aid extras (paw balm, vet wrap)

modules.title: Group gear
modules.why: a group of six or more

items.text: Large pot and a second stove or burner
Group tarp or canopy with poles and cord
Extra camp chairs and a folding table
Dish station: two tubs, soap, sponge, drying towel
Shared cooler plan and ice schedule
Two-way radios or a meeting-point plan
Gear and food assignment list
Trip plan and return time left with someone at home
Whistle and a signal mirror
Satellite messenger or personal locator beacon on remote trips
Spare phone battery and a printed map
Fishing license for the state or park
items.note: Check current seasons, limits and tackle rules.

items.text: Rod, reel and spare line
Tackle box: hooks, weights, lures or bait
Pliers and a line cutter
Net and a stringer or cooler with ice
Fillet knife and a cutting board
Helmet, harness and climbing shoes
Rope, belay device and locking carabiners
Rack: draws, cams or nuts for the routes planned
Chalk bag and tape
Guidebook or route topos downloaded
Approach shoes
Swimsuits and quick-dry towels
Water shoes or sandals
Life jackets for kids and weak swimmers
Dry bag for phone and keys
Goggles, floats or a paddleboard
Camera, lenses and lens cloth
Spare batteries and memory cards
Tripod
Dry bag or rain cover for the camera
Helmets
Pump, spare tube and a patch kit
Bike lock
Lights for dusk rides
Rack or straps to carry the bikes
Red-light headlamp or a red filter
Star chart or an offline sky app
Blanket or reclining chair
Binoculars
Extra warm layer for sitting still at night
Daypack
Map and compass, or offline maps
Water bottles or bladder (2 L per person)
Trail snacks
Trekking poles
Blister kit
Bear canister or hang kit as the area requires
items.note: Check current food-storage rules; many parks require approved canisters.

items.text: Bear spray where allowed, carried where you can reach it
items.note: Not allowed in some parks; check before you go.

items.text: Odour-proof bags for food, trash and toiletries
No food, wrappers or scented items in the tent
Sleeping bag rated 10°F (-12°C) colder than the forecast low, or a liner
Insulated sleeping pad (R-value 4 or more) or a second pad
Puffy jacket, warm hat and gloves
Insulated bottle for hot drinks
Extra stove fuel (cold air burns more)
Hand warmers
Dry sleep clothes kept in a sealed bag
Shade: tarp, canopy or a tent with a full fly
One gallon (4 L) of water per person per day, plus electrolytes
Wide-brim hat, sunglasses and a sun hoodie
Sunscreen SPF 30+ and lip balm
Cooler with plenty of ice
Misting bottle or a cooling towel
Plan to hike early and rest in the heat of the day
Rain jacket and rain pants
Tarp and cord for a dry cooking area
Pack cover or liner and dry bags
Extra socks and a dry set of camp clothes
Camp shoes that can get wet
Tent footprint, seam sealer and a sponge
Insect repellent (DEET or picaridin)
Head net
Permethrin-treated clothing
After-bite cream and antihistamine
Tick check comb and tweezers
Satellite messenger or personal locator beacon
Trip plan left with someone, with a check-in time
Paper maps and offline maps downloaded
Power bank and cables
Bigger first-aid kit: wound care, splint, blister care, meds
Spare car key kept by a second person

modules.title: Permits
modules.why: a permit or reservation is needed

items.text: Permit or reservation confirmation (printed and on the phone)
Photo ID for pickup or check-in
Pickup time, place and the ranger station hours
Entry pass or parking permit for the vehicle
Pitch the tent once at home
Test the stove and know how to light it
Arrive with daylight to spare
Pack a small repair kit: tape, cord, a multi-tool
Read the campground rules (quiet hours, fires, food storage)
Resupply plan: where and when
Laundry kit: soap, cord, clips
Extra fuel and a spare lighter
Spare batteries or a solar charger
Repair kit: patches, needle and thread, zip ties, duct tape
Cash for places that take nothing else
Firewood bought near the site (moving firewood spreads pests)
items.note: Check current fire restrictions before you leave.

items.text: Fire starter, matches and a lighter
Grill grate or a tripod
Cast-iron pan or dutch oven
Long tongs and heat-proof gloves
Hatchet or saw
Bucket and shovel to put the fire out
Foil, skewers and a roasting stick
Stove and enough fuel for every meal plus one day
Lighter and backup matches
Pot, pan and a lid
Utensils, spatula and a serving spoon
Plates, bowls, mugs
Dish soap, sponge and a wash basin
Trash bags and a hanging line for them
Cooler and ice (or a second cooler for drinks)
Ready-to-eat meals: wraps, salads, cold cuts, fruit
Plates, utensils and napkins
Trash bags
Thermos of hot drink from home
Water filter or purifier
Backup purification tablets
Bottles or bladder: 2 to 3 L per person
Collapsible container for camp water
Water jugs: one gallon (4 L) per person per day
Dispenser jug with a tap for camp
Refillable bottles for the car and hikes
Hammock with tree straps (wide straps protect bark)
Underquilt or sleeping pad for warmth underneath
Tarp with ridgeline and guy lines
Bug net
Carabiners and a drip line

modules.title: Sleeping in the vehicle
modules.why: sleeping in the vehicle or a rooftop tent

items.text: Mattress or sleeping platform that fits the vehicle
Window covers and bug screens
Levelling blocks or ramps
12 V fan or ventilation plan
Power station or a second battery for lights and devices
Organiser bins so gear does not take the bed
Reservation confirmation and the key or lock code
Bedding and towels if they are not provided
Indoor shoes or slippers
Lantern or flashlight for the walk from the car

modules.title: Tarp or bivy
modules.why: sleeping under a tarp or in a bivy

items.text: Bivy sack or tarp with poles, stakes and cord
Groundsheet
Bug net or head net
Tickets or wristbands and photo ID
Ear plugs
Cash and a card, split between two places
Portable charger and cables
Shade structure or a canopy with weights
Refillable bottle and a hydration pack
Wet wipes and hand sanitiser
Camp flag or totem so you can find your site
Costume, lights and a warm layer for the night
